title: Russians on a houseboat and the Italian New Orleans Jazz Band
summary: The Russians stayed on a Danube houseboat. An Italian group billed as a New Orleans jazz band followed the Straws everywhere and was amazed to meet real New Orleanians.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Oh, well, who was fighting? There wasn't any musicians fighting at all, huh? No.

Well, you see, uh, actually what happened, they, uh, they had, uh, a group from, uh, Israel. They had a group from Palestine. They had a group from Italy. You know, all the countries were represented, see. And, uh, naturally most of them were common, you see. Now, the true Russians themselves, the ones directly from, uh, Moscow and, uh, Leningrad and all, they stayed on a houseboat out in the Danube River. They didn't come on to festival grounds at all because they didn't want to have anybody say, well, the Russians caused this, you see. They wanted to keep as clear as possible, you see. In other words, let their little strong-on boys go out and do the work, you know. Uh, oh, that reminds me, speaking of this Italian group, they had a group over there, they called them the Italian New Orleans Jazz Band, so help me.
I know the manager, I think, the brother of the manager. Of this group?

Yeah. Well, anyway, uh, I don't know, it might have just been coincidence, but every place we played, these guys, these guys showed up right behind us. They were on the program, see. And every place we played, they were right behind us. And, uh, when they actually found out, well, we told them, we were from New Orleans, you see. And they thought we were handing them a line just like they handed everybody else a line in an Italian New Orleans Jazz Band, you see. But, uh, I mean, they were pretty well shocked when they actually found out that we were directly from New Orleans and we'd come there to play New Orleans music, you see. So I think they kind of hung around with us to pick up as much stuff as they could, you know, in our style of playing or what we do. On a bandstand or something like that, you know. But, uh, I mean, they were really amazed when they found out that we actually were from New Orleans.
